recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-17213; any future change to the operation definition itself belongs in the external CapabilityStatement IG, where the operation is currently Trial Use.
issue_request: FHIR-17213 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Conformance change request raised against STU3. It asked to remove normative treatment from the CapabilityStatement $implements operation because there had not been enough implementation experience; the approved resolution was to mark the operation as Trial Use ([TU]).
initial_application: The Jira comments say the change was already done in 2018. No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-17213 was found in the current repository history, but the tightly related broader issue FHIR-16072 records svn revision 14280 for marking the CapabilityStatement operations as TU. In current git history, the pre-R6 core source for operationdefinition-CapabilityStatement-implements.xml already carried structuredefinition-standards-status value trial-use.
additional_context: The current core build no longer defines CapabilityStatement.$implements in source/capabilitystatement. Commit 270e0ceb7b removed the core OperationDefinition-CapabilityStatement-implements source as part of the R6 normative cleanup, and current core prose only links to the external HL7/capstmt operation. The current external operation JSON reports structuredefinition-standards-status trial-use. Searches found no Zulip or Confluence evidence that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No core source edit is needed because the former core operation had already been demoted to Trial Use, and the current core source no longer owns the operation definition whose standards status was at issue.
